newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National to raise mortgage rate - report.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National to raise mortgage rate - report.

text.p: Britain's second largest housing finance lender Abbey National Plc will raise its variable mortgage rate by a quarter of one percentage point on Monday, according to the Times newspaper.
The move is a direct response to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's annual budget, the Times said.

The rate rise relates to the last quarter-point hike in bank base rates six weeks ago. At that time, most leading lenders adopted a wait-and-see policy until the government announced next year's spending plans to avoid to costly changes in quick succession, the Times said.
Abbey rates will rise to 7.29 percent for mortgages of up to 60,000 pounds and to 7.24 percent for mortgages of 60,000 to 100,000 pounds, the Times said.

As a verdict of Clarke's budget, announced last Tuesday, Abbey argues that it is moving now because the Chancellor's "cautious" spending plans made it unlikely that there would be another early rise in British base rates, the Times said.
Britain's base rate was increased from 5.75 percent to 6.00 percent on October 30.
The mortgage rate hike by Abbey National is likely to be followed by Britain's biggest housing lender, the Halifax, in the next two weeks, the Times said.

On Wednesday, the Halifax said it had no current plans to raise mortgage rates. But a Halifax spokesman said on Wednesday that the society would now watch market reaction to the budget and await any developments at the next monetary meeting between Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George on December 11.
In early November, the Nationwide Building Society but Britain's third-largest home lender was below the industry average. Halifax's standard variable rate currently stands at 6.99 percent.
